instrument: Purported 11 August 1976 Supreme Court Order / Writ of Execution
status: UNRESOLVED — CLAIMANT-SIDE DOCUMENTARY EXISTENCE CORROBORATED / SUPREME COURT DOCKET, ISSUANCE AUTHORITY, SIGNATURE, AND LEGAL-EFFECT AUTHENTICATION PENDING

evidence.finding: Lists an asserted ORIGINAL Supreme Court Order for Writ of Execution dated 11 August 1976.
evidence.weight: corroborates asserted existence; not independent judicial authentication

evidence.finding: Attributes the 11 August 1976 order to Chief Justice Fred Ruiz Castro and Judge Enrique A. Agana and reproduces claimed operative language.

evidence.source: Republic Petition for Annulment, Civil Case 3957-P / CA-G.R. SP 70014 materials
evidence.finding: Documents extensive government challenge to the authenticity/jurisdiction/reconstitution/enforcement of the 3957-P instrument chain.
evidence.weight: high-value adverse procedural evidence; underlying certified appellate record required

evidence.source: Philippine Supreme Court E-Library, G.R. Nos. 225353-54
evidence.finding: Records later enforcement controversy tied to LRC Civil Case 3957-P and an earlier Court of Appeals injunction against enforcement of an associated order.
evidence.weight: official corroboration that enforcement history is contested; does not independently authenticate the 11 Aug 1976 instrument

contradictions.issue: No exact Supreme Court docket bridge presently established for the alleged order.
Claimed dual signature by Chief Justice Castro and trial Judge Agana requires direct archival authentication.
Circulated international-jurisdiction language requires institutional and legal-capacity verification.
Later injunction/enforcement litigation prevents inference of present enforceability.
Original versus later reconstituted/certified-copy provenance must be separated.
